newsitem.title: TAIWAN: HK absent from Taiwan ruling party investment plan.
newsitem.headline: HK absent from Taiwan ruling party investment plan.

text.p: The business arm of Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party on Wednesday laid out its global investment priorities in a plan that deliberately avoids new projects in Hong Kong.

Party Business Management Committee chairman Liu Tai-ying, quoted by an aide, said Taiwan expected Hong Kong's stock and property markets to prosper in the near term after the British colony's July 1 handover to Taipei's arch rival, Beijing.
But Liu indicated the party was adopting a wait-and-see attitude toward Hong Kong's future under Chinese communist rule, saying party firms had no plans for new Hong Kong investments.

"If Hong Kong can remain stable, we can still use Hong Kong for our financial operations, but if it can't, we can conduct our financial operations in other financial centres like Tokyo or London," he said.
"In the longer run, Hong Kong's economy and markets will be affected by the Chinese communists' various economic and non-economic factors, and this is worth watching," he added.

Liu affirmed that the party, whose Republic of China government fled the mainland in 1949 after losing a civil war to the communists, had re-registered its Hong Kong businesses in Singapore in early 1997 to avoid risks.
The Nationalist Party, one of the world's richest with T$38 billion (US$1.4 billion) in assets, is among Taiwan's leading investors through its seven holding companies.
Liu said his party investments would focus on four sectors -- construction, high technology, petrochemicals and transport -- whether in Taiwan or abroad.
Liu noted that Taiwan's seven-year property slump finally was bottoming-out and said high-tech industries -- whether local or foreign -- were star performers.
